title: Every download route has a safe page
assertion: The registry test finds every `downloadHandler` route under `src/app` and refuses one without `returnTo`, one not registered at its file's path, and one whose page for synthetic IDs is not under its practice (the evidence export's under `/console/`); a page path of `//evil.example`, `/\evil.example`, `javascript:`, an absolute URL, encoded slashes, a control character, dot segments, a query, a fragment or an ID that is not opaque sends the navigation to `/`, as does a route with no page or a `returnTo` that throws; a kept value is dropped when its page's schema refuses it (a bad month returns to the monthly summary without it, and the page opens), when its name is not a lowercase code or is a refusal's own, or when it holds an identifier's shape, and no Location has a finding of the PHI guard; the page reads back only the closed codes and field names and ignores everything else; the codes field's pattern accepts exactly what the route accepts, letters with non-ASCII case mappings and Unicode separators included
noFileReason: The registry and every route.ts under src/app are read, and the hostile parameters and the codes are generated by the test; no file.
